question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The sound of elephants
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Trumpet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Trumpet is the standard one-word substitute for the loud, resonant cry made by an elephant. (हाथी की चिंघाड़)

◦ As a verb it is also used directly: The elephant trumpeted loudly in the forest.

◦ Correct: The sound of elephants is called a trumpet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Quack – the sound made by a duck, not an elephant. (बत्तख की आवाज़)

• Laurel – an aromatic evergreen shrub; "laurels" means honour or distinction, and is not a sound at all.

• Screech – a harsh, high-pitched shrill cry, typically of an owl, monkey or brakes, not of an elephant.

NOTE

• Common animal sounds asked in SSC exams: Lion – roar; Horse – neigh; Snake – hiss; Frog – croak; Bee – buzz.

• Dog – bark; Cow – low/moo; Wolf – howl; Crow – caw; Sheep – bleat; Donkey – bray.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Belieif.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The printed word "Belieif" is misspelt; the correct spelling is Belief – an acceptance that something is true or exists. (विश्वास, आस्था)

◦ It follows the classic spelling rule – "i" before "e" except after "c" – so it is bel-ie-f, with no extra "i".

◦ Correct: His belief in hard work never wavered.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shout – to call out loudly; correctly spelt. (चिल्लाना)

• Salute – to greet with a gesture of respect; correctly spelt. (सलामी देना)

• Crops – cultivated plants grown for food; correctly spelt. (फ़सलें)

NOTE

• Same "ie" family: relief, achieve, believe, grief, niece, piece.

• "ei" after c: receive, deceive, ceiling, perceive, receipt.

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: necessary, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, committee.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She was fined of driving over the speed limit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fined for driving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition that follows "fine" in the sense of punishing is for, not "of": *fined for something*. (जुर्माना लगाना)

◦ "Driving" is a gerund; a preposition is always followed by a gerund (V1+ing), never a bare infinitive. (क्रिया का संज्ञा रूप)

◦ Correct: She was fined for driving over the speed limit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fine of driving" drops the required passive past participle "fined" and keeps the wrong preposition.

• Option 2 "fined for drive" wrongly puts a bare infinitive after the preposition "for".

• Option 4 is wrong because the printed sentence does contain an error ("fined of").

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions: fined for, punished for, blamed for, scolded for, known for.

• Preposition + V-ing: "He is good at painting"; "She insisted on going"; "He is fond of singing".

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Aptitude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Talent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aptitude means a natural ability or capacity to learn or do something well. (योग्यता, प्रतिभा)

◦ Talent carries exactly this sense of an inborn skill or gift, so it is the closest synonym.

◦ Correct: She has a remarkable aptitude (talent) for mathematics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Attitude – a settled way of thinking or feeling about something; a mental outlook, not an ability. (रवैया)

• Stress – mental or emotional strain and tension. (तनाव)

• Faith – complete trust or confidence in someone or something. (आस्था, भरोसा)

NOTE

• Synonyms of aptitude: flair, knack, gift, faculty, capability, propensity.

• Antonyms of aptitude: inability, incapacity, ineptitude, clumsiness.

• Do not confuse aptitude (ability) with attitude (outlook) – a very common SSC trap pair.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

Apple has also introduced a (rule that seemed tie) to its recent dispute with Basecamp.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rule that seems tied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause uses the present perfect "has also introduced", so the relative clause must stay in the present tense – "that seems". (वर्तमान काल)

◦ The structure "be/seem + tied to" needs the past participle "tied", not the base verb "tie"; "tied to" means connected or linked to. (जुड़ा हुआ)

◦ Correct: Apple has also introduced a rule that seems tied to its recent dispute with Basecamp.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "rule that seemingly tied" turns "tied" into a finite past verb with an adverb, breaking the tense agreement and the sense.

• Option 3 is wrong because the bracketed part "rule that seemed tie" is ungrammatical ("seemed tie").

• Option 4 "rule which seemed tie" repeats the same error, keeping the base form "tie" after "seemed".

NOTE

• After linking verbs like seem, appear, look, become, use an adjective or a past participle, not a base verb.

• Useful collocation: tied to / linked to / related to / connected with + noun.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: The two are in most cases mutualy exclusive.
option_2: The two are in most cases mutualyy exclusive.
option_3: The two are in most cases mutually exclusive.
option_4: The two are in most casies mutually exclusive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The two are in most cases mutually exclusive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 3 spells both key words correctly – cases and mutually. (परस्पर, आपसी रूप से)

◦ Adjectives ending in -al form adverbs by adding -ly: mutual → mutual + ly = mutually (double "l").

◦ Correct: The two are in most cases mutually exclusive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mutualy" is misspelt – it drops one "l" from "mutually".

• Option 2 "mutualyy" is misspelt – it adds an extra "y" instead of the second "l".

• Option 4 "casies" is misspelt – the plural of "case" is cases, not "casies".

NOTE

• Similar -ally adverbs: actually, finally, especially, generally, occasionally, accidentally.

• "Mutually exclusive" means two things that cannot both be true or happen at the same time – a common phrase in reasoning and English papers.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

In humans, consumption of alcohol, stimulate brain cells to release mood-altering dopamine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. stimulate brain cells to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "consumption", which is singular, so the verb must also be singular – stimulates, not "stimulate". (कर्ता-क्रिया मेल)

◦ The phrase "of alcohol" is only a prepositional phrase; the verb never agrees with the noun inside such a phrase.

◦ Correct: In humans, consumption of alcohol stimulates brain cells to release mood-altering dopamine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "release mood-altering dopamine" is correct – a bare infinitive follows "to" in "to release".

• Option 2 "In humans, consumption of alcohol," contains no grammatical error.

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence clearly has a subject-verb agreement error.

NOTE

• Rule: Words between the subject and the verb (of, with, along with, as well as, together with, including) do not change the number of the verb.

• Example: The quality of the apples was poor. / The list of items is on the desk.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To stretch one's legs
option_1: To leave a place without permission
option_3: To go for a walk after you have been sitting for a long time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To go for a walk after you have been sitting for a long time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to stretch one's legs" means to go for a short walk, especially after sitting still for a long period. (टहलने जाना)

◦ It is typically used after a long journey, a long meeting or a long flight.

◦ Correct: After the six-hour train journey, we got down at the station to stretch our legs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "To leave a place without permission" is the meaning of to take French leave.

• "To go for a party" – not related to this idiom; "to paint the town red" means to go out and celebrate.

• "To measure one's worth" is closer to to take the measure of someone.

NOTE

• Other body-part idioms: to pull one's leg – to tease; to stand on one's own feet – to be independent.

• To put one's foot down – to be firm; to be all ears – to listen attentively.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I am looking forward to ______ you at our favourite restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. meeting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "look forward to", the word "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive, so it must be followed by a gerund (V1+ing). (उत्सुकता से प्रतीक्षा करना)

◦ Hence "looking forward to meeting", never "looking forward to meet".

◦ Correct: I am looking forward to meeting you at our favourite restaurant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "meets" is a finite present verb and cannot follow a preposition.

• Option 2 "meet" is a bare infinitive – the common trap in this question.

• Option 3 "met" is the past form and does not fit after the preposition "to".

NOTE

• Other phrases where "to" is a preposition and takes V-ing: be used to, get used to, accustomed to, addicted to, object to, with a view to, prone to, devoted to.

• Example: She is used to waking up early. / He objected to paying the fine.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

What evil magic does / it possess to draw the human / heart so powerful to it?
option_4: it possess to draw the human
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. heart so powerful to it?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word modifies the verb "draw", so it must be the adverb "powerfully", not the adjective "powerful". (क्रिया-विशेषण)

◦ Adjectives qualify nouns; adverbs qualify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs. Here "draw ... so powerfully" tells us *how* the heart is drawn.

◦ Correct: What evil magic does it possess to draw the human heart so powerfully to it?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "What evil magic does" is correct – standard interrogative word order with the auxiliary "does".

• Option 4 "it possess to draw the human" is correct because after the auxiliary "does" the bare infinitive "possess" is used.

• Option 3 is wrong since the sentence clearly contains an adjective-adverb error.

NOTE

• Similar adjective → adverb pairs: quick – quickly, careful – carefully, beautiful – beautifully, easy – easily.

• After "do/does/did", always use the V1 (bare) form: He does not know; She did not go.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Drastic times call for drastic measures
option_1: When you are extremely desperate you need to take extremely desperate actions
option_2: Don't rely on it until you sure of it
option_3: Something that ends at the last minute or last few seconds
option_4: Do not pull all your resources in one possibility
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. When you are extremely desperate you need to take extremely desperate actions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The proverb "Drastic times call for drastic measures" (also "desperate times call for desperate measures") means that extreme situations demand extreme, unusual action. (कठिन समय में कठोर कदम उठाने पड़ते हैं)

◦ It justifies taking a step one would normally avoid, because the circumstances are severe.

◦ Correct: The company sold half its assets to survive – after all, drastic times call for drastic measures.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Don't rely on it until you are sure of it" is closer to don't count your chickens before they hatch.

• "Something that ends at the last minute or last few seconds" describes a nail-biting finish / down to the wire.

• "Do not put all your resources in one possibility" is the sense of don't put all your eggs in one basket.

NOTE

• Drastic means severe, extreme and sudden in effect. (कठोर, अत्यधिक)

• Related proverbs: Necessity is the mother of invention; A stitch in time saves nine; Make hay while the sun shines.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

There is definitely ______ he is not telling me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an indefinite pronoun standing for an unspecified thing that is being withheld – something. (कुछ)

◦ In an affirmative sentence, "something" (not "anything") is the natural choice; "anything" belongs to negatives and questions.

◦ Correct: There is definitely something he is not telling me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Everything is too absolute – it would mean he tells her nothing at all, which contradicts "definitely".

• Somebody refers to a person, but the clause "he is not telling me" needs a *thing* (information) as its object.

• Anything is used mainly in negative sentences and questions: "He isn't telling me anything."

NOTE

• Rule: some- words (some, something, someone, somewhere) → affirmative sentences and polite offers/requests.

• any- words (any, anything, anyone, anywhere) → negatives, questions and conditional clauses.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Megan, my precious darling, where is the kettle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. detested.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In this sentence "precious" is used affectionately to mean greatly loved, dear or cherished. (प्रिय, अनमोल)

◦ Detested means intensely disliked or hated, which is the exact opposite of "loved/dear". (घृणित)

◦ Correct: The antonym of "precious" (dearly loved) here is detested.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Expensive – costing a lot of money; this is a synonym of "precious" in its monetary sense, not an antonym. (महँगा)

• Beloved – dearly loved; again a synonym of "precious" as used here. (प्यारा)

• Steep – sharply sloping, or (of a price) unreasonably high; not an antonym of "precious".

NOTE

• Synonyms of precious: cherished, treasured, valuable, invaluable, adored.

• Antonyms of precious: worthless, cheap, despised, hated, valueless.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

Immediate relocation is your best course of action.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. migration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Relocation means the act of moving to a new place to live or work. (स्थानांतरण)

◦ Migration likewise means movement from one place to another for settlement, so it is the closest synonym. (प्रवास)

◦ Correct: Immediate relocation (migration) is your best course of action.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Emergence – the process of coming into view or becoming known; unrelated to moving house. (उद्भव)

• Ending – the final part or conclusion of something. (अंत)

• Expiration – the coming to an end of a period of validity, as of a licence or document. (समाप्ति)

NOTE

• Synonyms of relocation: transfer, resettlement, shifting, displacement, transplantation.

• Related words: emigration (leaving one's own country), immigration (entering another country), evacuation (removal from danger).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Wicked
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Admirable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wicked means evil, morally wrong or cruel. (दुष्ट, बुरा)

◦ Admirable means deserving respect and approval – the direct opposite of being evil or wicked. (प्रशंसनीय)

◦ Correct: His wicked deeds were the very opposite of his brother's admirable conduct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sarcastic – using irony to mock or convey contempt; not the opposite of wicked. (व्यंग्यात्मक)

• Infernal – relating to hell, devilish or damnable; this is a synonym of wicked, not an antonym. (नारकीय)

• Dissent – disagreement with a prevailing opinion; a noun/verb, not an antonym of wicked. (असहमति)

NOTE

• Synonyms of wicked: evil, vile, immoral, sinful, villainous, nefarious.

• Antonyms of wicked: virtuous, righteous, noble, moral, upright, benevolent.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

All the companies make an ______ to be seen and heard within communities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. effort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "make an effort (to do something)" – to try hard to achieve something. (प्रयास करना)

◦ The infinitive "to be seen and heard" fits naturally after "effort", showing purpose.

◦ Correct: All the companies make an effort to be seen and heard within communities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Establishment – a business, organisation or the act of setting one up; "make an establishment to be seen" is not idiomatic. (स्थापना)

• Excuse – a reason offered to justify a fault; "make an excuse" exists but reverses the intended positive sense. (बहाना)

• Aisle – a passage between rows of seats or shelves; completely unrelated in meaning. (गलियारा)

NOTE

• Common "make" collocations: make an effort, make a decision, make progress, make a mistake, make arrangements, make a difference.

• Common "do" collocations: do homework, do business, do a favour, do research, do one's duty.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Since 1950 the number of children in secondary schools has been increasing noticeable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has been increasing noticeably.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Increasing" is a verb form, so it must be modified by the adverb "noticeably", not the adjective "noticeable". (ध्यान देने योग्य ढंग से)

◦ "Since 1950" demands the present perfect continuous – *has been increasing* – and "the number of" takes a singular verb (has). (काल का नियम)

◦ Correct: Since 1950 the number of children in secondary schools has been increasing noticeably.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the printed sentence uses the adjective "noticeable" where an adverb is needed.

• Option 2 "have increasingly noticeably" uses the plural "have" with the singular subject "the number" and stacks two adverbs meaninglessly.

• Option 4 "increasingly noticeable" removes the verb altogether, leaving the sentence without a predicate.

NOTE

• The number of + plural noun → singular verb; A number of + plural noun → plural verb.

• With since / for, use the present perfect or present perfect continuous: He has been working here since 2010.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Jacqueline represents retirement as the final result of a long course of dissatisfaction with ______ life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. mundane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence speaks of "dissatisfaction", so the blank needs a word with a dull, negative shade – mundane, meaning dull, ordinary and lacking excitement. (नीरस, सांसारिक)

◦ A mundane life is exactly the kind of routine existence that would create long-standing dissatisfaction leading to retirement.

◦ Correct: Jacqueline represents retirement as the final result of a long course of dissatisfaction with mundane life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Joyful – full of happiness; contradicts "dissatisfaction". (आनंदमय)

• Barbaric – savagely cruel and uncivilised; far too extreme for ordinary working life. (बर्बर)

• Divine – of or like God, heavenly; a positive word that clashes with the negative tone. (दिव्य)

NOTE

• Synonyms of mundane: banal, humdrum, routine, tedious, prosaic, unexciting.

• Antonyms of mundane: extraordinary, exciting, remarkable, heavenly, spiritual.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I spend a lot of my time at work helping my customers find an best outfit.
option_3: my time at work helping my
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. customers find an best outfit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A superlative degree ("best") is always preceded by the definite article "the", never by "a/an". (सर्वोत्तम – निश्चित उपवाक्य)

◦ Moreover, "an" is used only before a vowel sound, and "best" begins with the consonant sound /b/, so "an best" is doubly wrong.

◦ Correct: I spend a lot of my time at work helping my customers find the best outfit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "I spend a lot of" is correct – simple present for a habitual action.

• Option 3 "my time at work helping my" is correct – "spend time + V-ing" is the standard structure.

• Option 1 is wrong because the sentence clearly contains an article error.

NOTE

• Rule: the + superlative – the tallest boy, the most beautiful painting, the worst result.

• Article by sound, not spelling: an hour, an MP, a university, a one-rupee coin.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Departure from common rule
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Anomaly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An anomaly is something that deviates from what is standard, normal or expected – a departure from the common rule. (असंगति, विसंगति)

◦ It is the standard one-word substitute for an irregularity or exception to a rule.

◦ Correct: A departure from the common rule is called an anomaly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Quixotic – extremely idealistic and unrealistic, chasing impractical ideals (from Don Quixote). (काल्पनिक, अव्यावहारिक)

• Pragmatic – dealing with things in a practical, realistic way. (व्यावहारिक)

• Stupor – a state of near-unconsciousness or dazed insensibility. (मूर्च्छा, बेहोशी)

NOTE

• Synonyms of anomaly: aberration, irregularity, deviation, abnormality, oddity, exception.

• Related one-word substitutes: Nonconformist – one who does not follow accepted rules; Heretic – one who opposes established religious belief.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for (1) ______. They travelled by boat to the coastal towns of Seward and Knik, and from there by land into the gold fields. The trail they used to (2) ______ inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail, one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress of the United States. The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail. People also used it to get from place to place, including the priests, ministers, and judges who had to travel between villages. In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. gold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The very next sentence says the settlers went "by land into the gold fields", which directly confirms that they came to Alaska looking for gold. (सोना)

◦ This period refers to the famous Alaska gold rush of the early twentieth century.

◦ Correct: In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for gold.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Copper, iron and silver are all metals, but none of them is mentioned anywhere in the passage.

• The passage's internal clue "gold fields" makes gold the only contextually supported choice.

• In cloze tests, the answer is almost always confirmed by a repeated word or synonym in a neighbouring sentence.

NOTE

• Strategy for cloze passages: read the whole passage once, then fill the easiest blanks first and use nearby lexical clues.

• Watch for collocations and repetition – they signal the intended word far more reliably than general knowledge.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for (1) ______. They travelled by boat to the coastal towns of Seward and Knik, and from there by land into the gold fields. The trail they used to (2) ______ inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail, one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress of the United States. The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail. People also used it to get from place to place, including the priests, ministers, and judges who had to travel between villages. In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. travel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows "The trail they used to (2) ______ inland", so it needs a verb of movement – people used the trail to travel inland. (यात्रा करना)

◦ "Travel" collocates naturally with trail, road and route, and the passage itself later repeats "means of travel down this trail".

◦ Correct: The trail they used to travel inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Submerge – to go under water; makes no sense for an inland land trail.

• Locate – to find the exact position of something; it needs an object, and "locate inland" is not idiomatic.

• Navigate – usually used for steering ships or aircraft along a planned route; it is transitive here and less apt than "travel" for a land trail.

NOTE

• Note the structure "used to + V1" and the collocation "travel inland" (towards the interior of a country).

• Useful travel collocations: travel by boat, travel overland, travel across, means of travel.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for (1) ______. They travelled by boat to the coastal towns of Seward and Knik, and from there by land into the gold fields. The trail they used to (2) ______ inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail, one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress of the United States. The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail. People also used it to get from place to place, including the priests, ministers, and judges who had to travel between villages. In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress" is in the passive voice, and the agent (doer) in a passive construction is introduced by the preposition by. (द्वारा)

◦ Structure: past participle + by + agent → "designated by the Congress of the United States".

◦ Correct: ... one of the National Historic Trails designated by the Congress of the United States.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• In shows position or enclosure and cannot introduce the doer of a passive verb.

• Of indicates possession or relation, not agency.

• At indicates a specific point of place or time, which does not fit here.

NOTE

• Passive-voice rule: object + be + V3 + by + subject – The letter was written by him.

• Use with for the instrument and by for the agent: The cake was cut by her with a knife.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for (1) ______. They travelled by boat to the coastal towns of Seward and Knik, and from there by land into the gold fields. The trail they used to (2) ______ inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail, one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress of the United States. The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail. People also used it to get from place to place, including the priests, ministers, and judges who had to travel between villages. In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. carried.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes how "the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail" – they were carried across it, i.e. taken from one place to another along the trail. (ले जाया गया)

◦ "Carried across" is the natural collocation with a trail or path; it also explains why the trail became a major thoroughfare.

◦ Correct: The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were carried across this trail.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Deported – to expel a person from a country; it is never used for mail or goods.

• Imported – to bring goods into a country from abroad; the trail is used within Alaska, not across national borders.

• Transported is close in meaning, but it normally takes "to/from" rather than "across a trail"; the official key is "carried".

NOTE

• Collocations: carry mail, carry supplies, carry goods across/along.

• Distinguish: export (send out), import (bring in), deport (expel a person), transport (move goods by vehicle).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In the early 1920's, settlers came to Alaska looking for (1) ______. They travelled by boat to the coastal towns of Seward and Knik, and from there by land into the gold fields. The trail they used to (2) ______ inland is known today as the Iditarod Trail, one of the National Historic Trails designated (3) ______ the Congress of the United States. The Iditarod Trail quickly became a major thoroughfare in Alaska, as the mail and supplies were (4) ______ across this trail. People also used it to get from place to place, including the priests, ministers, and judges who had to travel between villages. In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A dog sled is a vehicle pulled by dogs over snow – exactly the winter means of travel described in the passage. (कुत्तों द्वारा खींची जाने वाली स्लेज)

◦ The words "In the winter" and "means of travel" together point to a vehicle, and the Iditarod Trail is world-famous for its dog-sled race.

◦ Correct: In the winter, the settlers' only means of travel down this trail was via dog sled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Smell – a sense or odour; "via dog smell" is meaningless as a means of travel.

• Bark – the sound made by a dog; again not a mode of transport.

• Boat – already mentioned earlier for coastal travel, and boats cannot be used on a snow-covered inland trail in winter.

NOTE

• The Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race is run annually in Alaska from Anchorage to Nome – a fact often used in comprehension passages.

• Snow vocabulary: sled/sledge/sleigh (snow vehicle), mush (to drive a dog sled), thoroughfare (a main road or route).

question: Which of the following personality is associated with Aligarh movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmed Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aligarh Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in the second half of the 19th century to promote modern, Western scientific education among Indian Muslims. (अलीगढ़ आंदोलन — सर सैय्यद अहमद खां)

• He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh in 1875, which became the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in 1920.

• He also started the journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq and wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (The Causes of the Indian Revolt).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Muhammad Ali Jinnah — leader of the Muslim League and founder of Pakistan; called the *Quaid-e-Azam*.

• Abul Kalam Azad — freedom fighter, Congress President (1923, 1940–46) and India's first Education Minister; his birthday, 11 November, is National Education Day.

• Syed Amir Ali — jurist and author of *The Spirit of Islam*; founded the Central National Muhammadan Association (1877).

NOTE

• Socio-religious reform movements: Brahmo Samaj — Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1828); Arya Samaj — Dayanand Saraswati (1875); Prarthana Samaj — Atmaram Pandurang (1867); Ramakrishna Mission — Swami Vivekananda (1897).

question: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was started in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was launched on 15 July 2015 (World Youth Skills Day) by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना)

• It is the flagship skill-certification scheme, implemented through the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), giving free short-term training and recognition of prior learning (RPL) to youth.

• It has run in phases — PMKVY 1.0 (2015), 2.0 (2016–20), 3.0 (2020) and 4.0 (announced in Budget 2023).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 2014 — launch year of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Make in India, Swachh Bharat Mission and Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana.

• 2016 — launch year of Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, Startup India and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.

• The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship itself was created in November 2014.

NOTE

• World Youth Skills Day — 15 July, declared by the UN General Assembly in 2014.

• Other skill schemes: DDU-GKY, Skill India Mission (2015), SANKALP and STRIVE.

question: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodh gaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (nirvana/bodhi) under a peepal (Bodhi) tree on the bank of the Niranjana (Falgu) river at Bodh Gaya, in present-day Bihar. (बोधगया — ज्ञान प्राप्ति स्थल)

• He was born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini and attained enlightenment at the age of 35.

• The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2002).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Varanasi (Sarnath) — where the Buddha delivered his first sermon, the *Dharmachakra Pravartana*.

• Kushinagar (UP) — where he attained Mahaparinirvana (death) in 483 BC.

• Ujjain — ancient capital of the Avanti Mahajanapada, famous for the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga; Pataliputra — capital of Magadha under the Mauryas.

NOTE

• Buddha's life events and their symbols: Birth — lotus/bull; Enlightenment — Bodhi tree; First sermon — wheel (Dharmachakra); Death — stupa.

• Buddhist councils: 1st — Rajgriha (483 BC), 2nd — Vaishali (383 BC), 3rd — Pataliputra (250 BC, Ashoka), 4th — Kundalvana, Kashmir (Kanishka).

question: The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple was constructed in 999 A.D. by the king Dhangadeva of ______ dynasty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandela.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple at Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh) is the largest and most ornate temple of the group, built around 999 AD by the Chandela ruler Dhangadeva. (चंदेल वंश)

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is built in the Nagara style of temple architecture.

• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pala dynasty — ruled Bengal and Bihar; founder Gopala; patrons of Buddhism and of Nalanda and Vikramshila universities.

• Pallava dynasty — ruled from Kanchipuram; built the Shore Temple and Rathas at Mahabalipuram.

• Chola dynasty — built the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur (Rajaraja I) in the Dravidian style.

NOTE

• Temple styles: Nagara (North India, curvilinear shikhara), Dravida (South India, pyramidal vimana with gopurams), Vesara (Deccan, hybrid).

• Other Chandela sites: Lakshmana Temple, Vishvanatha Temple and the Chausath Yogini Temple at Khajuraho.

question: As on 1st March 2023, which of the following is NOT a member country of ASEAN?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) was founded on 8 August 1967 by the Bangkok Declaration; its headquarters is at Jakarta, Indonesia. (आसियान)

• It has 10 members: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand (the five founders), plus Brunei (1984), Vietnam (1995), Laos and Myanmar (1997) and Cambodia (1999).

• Sri Lanka is a South Asian country, not a Southeast Asian one, and is therefore not an ASEAN member.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sri Lanka is a member of SAARC, BIMSTEC and the IORA.

• India is not a member of ASEAN; it is a dialogue partner (full dialogue partner since 1996) and a member of the East Asia Summit.

• Timor-Leste was granted in-principle admission as ASEAN's 11th member in 2022 and became a full member later.

NOTE

• SAARC — formed 1985, HQ Kathmandu, 8 members. BIMSTEC — formed 1997, HQ Dhaka, 7 members.

• ASEAN motto: “One Vision, One Identity, One Community”.

question: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, was formerly known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Victoria Terminus Station.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai was formerly called Victoria Terminus (VT), named after Queen Victoria and opened in 1887. (विक्टोरिया टर्मिनस)

• It was designed by the British architect F. W. Stevens in the Victorian Gothic Revival style blended with Indian traditional elements.

• It was renamed Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus in 1996 and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in 2017; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2004).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• CSMT is the headquarters of the Central Railway.

• India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane, a distance of 34 km.

• Other renamed stations: Habibganj → Rani Kamlapati (Bhopal), Mughalsarai → Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction.

NOTE

• UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Maharashtra: Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Elephanta Caves, CSMT and the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai.

• Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones; the largest zone by route length is the Northern Railway.

question: Chhau dance is a blend of martial traditions, temple rituals etc. It is performed in which region of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eastern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical masked dance of eastern India, blending martial arts, tribal traditions and temple rituals. (छाऊ नृत्य)

• It has three recognised styles named after their places of origin — Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

• Chhau was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Purulia and Seraikella styles use masks, while Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks.

• Themes are drawn from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore; the Chaitra Parva festival is its main occasion.

• Other eastern folk dances: Bihu (Assam), Jhumar (Jharkhand) and Ghumura (Odisha).

NOTE

• India's 8 classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Other Indian entries on the UNESCO ICH list: Kutiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Kalbelia, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata and Garba of Gujarat.

question: The Indian Census 2011 can be referred to as the ______ census operation after Indian independence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is seventh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census since 1872 and the 7th census after Independence. (स्वतंत्रता के बाद सातवीं जनगणना)

• Post-independence censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1971, 1981, 1991, 2001 and 2011 — seven in all.

• The census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs; its motto in 2011 was “Our Census, Our Future”.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first census in India was attempted in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first complete/synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

• Census 2011 data: population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons/km².

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest — Bihar.

NOTE

• Census is a Union subject, listed at Entry 69 of the Union List in the Seventh Schedule.

• Highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest — Haryana (879); highest density — Bihar (1106).

question: Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indus valley civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization (c. 2500–1750 BC) was the first ancient Indian civilization with systematic town planning, using the grid pattern with streets cutting each other at right angles. (सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता)

• Its outstanding feature was an elaborate underground/covered drainage system with brick-lined drains, manholes and soak pits — unmatched in the ancient world.

• Cities were divided into a raised citadel and a lower town, built with standardised burnt bricks in the ratio 4:2:1.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Later Vedic civilization was largely rural and agrarian, with no comparable urban planning.

• The Aegean civilization (Minoan and Mycenaean, Greece) and the Nubian civilization (Africa) lie outside India.

• Key sites: Harappa (Daya Ram Sahni, 1921), Mohenjodaro (R. D. Banerji, 1922), Lothal (dockyard), Kalibangan (ploughed field), Dholavira (water reservoirs, UNESCO 2021).

NOTE

• The Great Bath was found at Mohenjodaro; the Great Granary at Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

• The Harappan script is pictographic and written boustrophedon (right to left in the first line, then left to right); it is still undeciphered.

question: What does Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code signifies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Criminalize unnatural offences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 dealt with “unnatural offences” — carnal intercourse against the order of nature. (अप्राकृतिक अपराध)

• In Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018), a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court decriminalised consensual homosexual acts between adults, reading down Section 377.

• The section still applies to non-consensual acts and bestiality.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Triple talaq — struck down in Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017); criminalised by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

• Surrogacy — regulated by the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021, which permits only altruistic surrogacy.

• Women's temple entry — the Sabarimala judgment (Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala, 2018) allowed women of all ages to enter the shrine.

NOTE

• The IPC, 1860 was drafted on the recommendation of the First Law Commission under Lord Macaulay and came into force in 1862.

• The IPC has been replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, effective from 1 July 2024.

question: वायुमंडल की निम्नलिखित परतों में से किसका अर्थ "मिश्रण का क्षेत्र (region of mixing)" है?
solution_text:
The correct answer is क्षोभमंडल (Troposphere).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word Troposphere comes from the Greek *tropos*, meaning “mixing” or “turning” — hence it is called the region of mixing. (क्षोभमंडल — मिश्रण का क्षेत्र)

• It is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, extending to about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator, and contains nearly 75% of the atmosphere's mass and almost all its water vapour.

• All weather phenomena — clouds, rain, fog, storms — occur here; temperature falls with height at about 6.5°C per km (normal lapse rate). Its upper limit is the tropopause.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Stratosphere (समताप मंडल) — contains the ozone layer; ideal for jet aircraft flying because it is cloud-free and stable.

• Mesosphere (मध्यमंडल) — the coldest layer (about –80°C at the mesopause); meteors burn up here.

• Thermosphere (बाह्य वायुमंडल) — contains the ionosphere, which reflects radio waves back to earth; auroras occur here.

NOTE

• Order of layers from the surface: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere.

• Composition of air: Nitrogen 78%, Oxygen 21%, Argon 0.93%, Carbon dioxide 0.04%.

question: Shovana Narayan is a renowned ________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shovana Narayan is a celebrated Kathak exponent and a disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj of the Lucknow gharana. (कथक नृत्यांगना)

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1992) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1999–2000); she also served as an officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service.

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from *katha* (story); it is known for chakkars (spins), intricate footwork (tatkar) and the use of *ghungroos*.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Manipuri — Manipur; exponents: Guru Bipin Singh, Jhaveri Sisters, Nirmala Mehta.

• Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; exponents: Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Vempati Chinna Satyam.

• Odissi — Odisha; exponents: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi.

NOTE

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow (expression/bhava), Jaipur (footwork/technique) and Banaras.

• Other famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Gopi Krishna, Kumudini Lakhia, Uma Sharma.

question: The Mahanadi river rises in the highlands of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh, near Sihawa in the Dhamtari district, and flows east through Odisha into the Bay of Bengal. (महानदी)

• It is about 851 km long, and is famous for the Hirakud Dam in Odisha — India's longest dam, built across it.

• Its main tributaries are the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib, Jonk and Tel; it forms a large delta near Cuttack.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• East-flowing peninsular rivers into the Bay of Bengal: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Subarnarekha, Penna.

• Godavari — rises at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik (Maharashtra); called the Dakshina Ganga, longest peninsular river.

• Krishna — rises at Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra); Kaveri — rises at Talakaveri, Brahmagiri hills (Karnataka).

NOTE

• West-flowing peninsular rivers: Narmada (Amarkantak) and Tapi (Multai), both forming estuaries, not deltas.

• The Mahanadi water dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

question: When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1575.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Tukaroi was fought on 3 March 1575 between the Mughal forces of Akbar, led by Munim Khan, and Daud Khan Karrani, the Sultan of Bengal and Bihar. (तुकारोई का युद्ध)

• It was fought at Tukaroi in the Balasore district of present-day Odisha, and ended in a decisive Mughal victory, leading to the Treaty of Cuttack.

• Daud Khan later rebelled and was finally defeated and killed at the Battle of Rajmahal (1576), ending the Karrani dynasty and completing the Mughal annexation of Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1564 — Akbar abolished the jizya (pilgrimage tax had been abolished in 1563).

• 1582 — Akbar proclaimed Din-i-Ilahi, his syncretic faith.

• 1576 — the Battle of Haldighati between Akbar's forces (Man Singh) and Maharana Pratap.

NOTE

• Akbar's key battles: Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu; Battle of Thanesar (1567); Siege of Chittor (1568); Battle of Haldighati (1576).

• Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system and the Dahsala/Zabti (Todar Mal) revenue system.

question: Who were the prime accused in the Assembly bomb case that took place in 1929, Delhi?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Mangal';src: url('https://appxcontent.kaxa.in/fonts/MANGAL.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Udham Singh and Mangal Pandey
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal bombs and leaflets in the Central Legislative Assembly, Delhi, protesting against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill. (केंद्रीय असेंबली बम कांड)

• They did not flee — they shouted “Inquilab Zindabad” and courted arrest, saying “it takes a loud voice to make the deaf hear.”

• Both belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940 to avenge the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; Mangal Pandey began the Revolt of 1857 at Barrackpore.

• Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930).

• Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla Khan were hanged in 1927 for the Kakori Conspiracy (1925).

NOTE

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case (Saunders murder); the day is observed as Shaheed Diwas.

• Bhagat Singh wrote “Why I am an Atheist” and founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926).

question: ______ is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishakhapatnam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Visakhapatnam Port (Andhra Pradesh) is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port in India, situated on the east coast along the Bay of Bengal. (विशाखापत्तनम बंदरगाह)

• The port was originally developed for the export of iron ore and handles a large volume of crude oil and general cargo; it also houses a shipbuilding yard (Hindustan Shipyard).

• It is the headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command of the Indian Navy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kandla (Deendayal Port), Gujarat — a tidal port in the Gulf of Kachchh, developed after Partition to replace Karachi; a free trade zone port.

• Mumbai Port — a natural harbour and India's oldest major port; Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) is the largest container port.

• Paradip (Odisha) — an artificial deep-water port at the confluence of the Mahanadi and the Bay of Bengal, exporting iron ore to Japan.

NOTE

• India has 13 major ports — 6 on the east coast (Kolkata, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Kamarajar/Ennore, V.O. Chidambaranar/Tuticorin) and the rest on the west coast plus Port Blair.

• Kolkata is India's only riverine major port; Kochi is a natural harbour on the Malabar coast.

question: The famous Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is located in the Tirupati (earlier Nellore) district of Andhra Pradesh, close to the Andhra–Tamil Nadu border. (नेलापट्टू पक्षी अभयारण्य)

• It is one of the largest breeding grounds for spot-billed pelicans in South-East Asia, and also hosts painted storks, herons and open-billed storks.

• The sanctuary lies near the Pulicat Lake ecosystem and hosts an annual Flamingo Festival.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other sanctuaries of Andhra Pradesh: Kolleru Lake, Pulicat Lake, Coringa, Rollapadu, Sri Venkateswara and Papikonda National Park.

• Tamil Nadu — Vedanthangal (oldest bird sanctuary in India), Point Calimere, Koonthankulam.

• Karnataka — Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary; Madhya Pradesh — Karera and the Ramsar site Bhoj Wetland.

NOTE

• Famous bird sanctuaries: Keoladeo Ghana (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) — a UNESCO site and Ramsar site; Chilika (Odisha) — largest brackish-water lagoon; Sultanpur (Haryana); Nal Sarovar (Gujarat).

• Pulicat Lake is India's second-largest brackish-water lagoon, shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

question: Who among the following is a celebrated sarod maestro?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zarin Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Zarin Daruwala Sharma was a celebrated Indian sarod player, one of the very few women to attain mastery over the instrument. (सरोद वादक)

• She trained under Pandit Haripada Ghosh and Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, and was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• The sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument of Hindustani classical music, known for its deep, weighty sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Niladri Kumar — a sitar player, known for inventing the electric “zitar”.

• Ustad Vilayat Khan — a legendary sitar maestro of the Imdadkhani gharana.

• N. Ramani — a renowned Carnatic flute (venu) player, awarded the Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Famous sarod maestros: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan, Allauddin Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta.

• Instrument–artist pairs: Sitar — Ravi Shankar; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla — Zakir Hussain; Violin — L. Subramaniam; Mohan Veena — Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

question: The GDP estimation method measuring the aggregate value of factor payments is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is income method.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The income method estimates national income by adding up the aggregate of factor payments — rent, wages, interest and profit — earned by the factors of production (land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship). (आय विधि)

• It gives NDP at factor cost = Compensation of employees + Operating surplus + Mixed income of self-employed.

• It is also known as the factor income method or distributed share method.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Product / value added method — adds the gross value added by all producing units, avoiding double counting by subtracting intermediate consumption.

• Expenditure method — GDP = C + I + G + (X – M), i.e. consumption, investment, government spending and net exports.

• All three methods must, in theory, give the same value of national income.

NOTE

• National income estimates in India are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

• The first estimate of national income in India was made by Dadabhai Naoroji in *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*; the first scientific estimate was by Prof. V. K. R. V. Rao. The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: In India, the practice of erecting megaliths began about ________ ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3000 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India the practice of erecting megaliths began about 3000 years ago (roughly 1000 BC), in the Iron Age. (महापाषाण संस्कृति)

• Megaliths are large stone structures erected over or around burials; the word comes from Greek *mega* (big) and *lithos* (stone).

• They are found mainly in the Deccan, South India (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh), the North-East and Kashmir; typical types are cists, dolmens, menhirs, cairn circles and urn burials.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Megalithic burials commonly contain iron tools and weapons, Black-and-Red Ware (BRW) pottery, horse equipment, and beads.

• Important megalithic sites: Brahmagiri and Maski (Karnataka), Adichanallur (Tamil Nadu), Junapani (Maharashtra) and Burzahom (Kashmir).

• The presence of grave goods suggests a belief in life after death and social differentiation.

NOTE

• Prehistoric periods: Palaeolithic → Mesolithic → Neolithic → Chalcolithic → Iron Age.

• Bhimbetka (MP) — famous rock shelters with prehistoric paintings, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2003).

question: Which among the following elements does not belongs to the Halogens group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helium (He) is a noble/inert gas belonging to Group 18 of the periodic table, not to the halogens. (उत्कृष्ट गैस)

• The halogens form Group 17 and include Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), Astatine (At) and Tennessine (Ts). *Halogen* means “salt-producing.”

• Halogens have 7 electrons in their outermost shell and are highly reactive non-metals, whereas noble gases have a completely filled outer shell and are chemically inert.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fluorine is the most reactive and the most electronegative element; Astatine is radioactive.

• Bromine is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature; Mercury is the only liquid metal.

• Helium is the second-lightest element, has the lowest boiling point of any element, and is used in weather balloons, airships and in cryogenics/MRI machines.

NOTE

• Group names: Group 1 — alkali metals; Group 2 — alkaline earth metals; Group 17 — halogens; Group 18 — noble gases.

• The modern periodic table is based on Moseley's Modern Periodic Law — properties are a periodic function of atomic number.

question: As announced in the Budget 2022, ________ Anganwadis will be upgraded for improving child health.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 lakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2022–23, presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2022, it was announced that 2 lakh Anganwadis would be upgraded to Saksham Anganwadis. (सक्षम आंगनवाड़ी)

• Saksham Anganwadis are a new generation of centres with better infrastructure, audio-visual aids and clean energy, providing improved child health and nutrition services.

• They come under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Anganwadi system was started under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, launched on 2 October 1975.

• Budget 2022–23 also announced PM GatiShakti, the Digital Rupee (CBDC), 75 digital banking units, PM-DevINE and the Vibrant Villages Programme.

• Umbrella schemes for women and children: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya and Mission Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the Annual Financial Statement.

• Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission) was launched on 8 March 2018 from Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan.

question: Which among the following team won the International Cricket Council (ICC) Men's T20 World Cup 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Australia won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021, beating New Zealand by 8 wickets in the final at Dubai on 14 November 2021. (टी20 विश्व कप 2021)

• It was Australia's first ever Men's T20 World Cup title; Mitchell Marsh (77*) was the Player of the Match and David Warner the Player of the Tournament.

• The tournament was hosted by India but shifted to the UAE and Oman because of COVID-19.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• England won the T20 World Cup 2010 and 2022 (beating Pakistan in the 2022 final at Melbourne).

• West Indies are the only team to win it twice — 2012 and 2016.

• India won the first-ever T20 World Cup in 2007 in South Africa under MS Dhoni, beating Pakistan, and won again in 2024 under Rohit Sharma.

NOTE

• T20 World Cup winners: 2007 India, 2009 Pakistan, 2010 England, 2012 & 2016 West Indies, 2014 Sri Lanka, 2021 Australia, 2022 England, 2024 India.

• ICC headquarters — Dubai, UAE; it was founded in 1909 as the Imperial Cricket Conference.

question: "Wide Angle" is an autobiography of which of the following sportsperson?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anil Kumble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Wide Angle” is the autobiography of the former Indian leg-spinner and captain Anil Kumble. (आत्मकथा)

• Kumble is India's highest wicket-taker in Test cricket (619 wickets) and one of only two bowlers in history to take all 10 wickets in a Test innings — 10/74 against Pakistan at Delhi in 1999 (the other being Jim Laker).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

• Wasim Akram — *Sultan: A Memoir*.

• Yuvraj Singh — *The Test of My Life*, on his battle with cancer.

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies: Playing It My Way — Sachin Tendulkar; A Century Is Not Enough — Sourav Ganguly; Unbreakable — Mary Kom; Ace Against Odds — Sania Mirza; Straight from the Heart — Kapil Dev; Race of My Life — Milkha Singh.

question: Which religious group of people celebrates the Nowruz festival in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parsis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nowruz (Navroz) is celebrated in India mainly by the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community as their New Year. (नवरोज़ — पारसी नव वर्ष)

• The word Nowruz is Persian for “new day”; it marks the spring equinox (around 21 March), though Parsis in India following the Shahenshahi calendar observe Jamshedi Navroz in March and their New Year in August.

• Nowruz was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2009, expanded 2016); the UN observes 21 March as International Nowruz Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other Parsi observances: Pateti (day of repentance preceding the New Year) and Khordad Sal (birthday of Prophet Zarathustra).

• Jews celebrate Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Hanukkah; Buddhists celebrate Buddha Purnima (Vesak) and Losar.

• Jains celebrate Mahavir Jayanti, Paryushana and Das Lakshana.

NOTE

• Zoroastrianism was founded by Prophet Zarathustra; its holy book is the Zend Avesta and its places of worship are fire temples (Agiary); the Tower of Silence (Dakhma) is used for the disposal of the dead.

• Parsis migrated to India (Sanjan, Gujarat) around the 8th–10th century AD from Persia.
